title: Palworld
notes: Played at the base camp — the same spot for every measurement — at 1920x1080 borderless fullscreen, across three sessions today: one DXVK run (~7 min, black 3D scene) and two d3dmetal runs (~16 min total, working normally). Frame rates read off the Metal HUD, all at the base camp: - highest preset, no DLSS: ~15 fps - medium preset + DLSS Performance: 30.0 fps - low preset + DLSS Performance: 32.5 fps So DLSS Performance was worth about +104%, and dropping medium to low only +8%. While playing I sampled the machine: the GPU's "Device Utilization %" stayed pinned at 100 across three samples, while the game's own CPU use sat near 6% of one core — GPU-bound, not CPU-bound. Memory was tight as well: 19.6 GB in use across the machine against 16 GB of RAM, swap at 4.77 / 5.12 GB. DLSS needs two switches on at once: "Enable DLSS (MetalFX)" in the environment's Graphics section, and DLSS itself in the game's own video settings. Confirmed live from the launch log line WINEDLLOVERRIDES=nvapi64,nvngx=n,b. With DLSS on, the game's settings also grow an "NVIDIA Reflex low latency" entry — D3DMetal's nvngx bridge makes the game see an NVIDIA card.
issues: Launching from the Steam client window instead of Highball's own library gives a black 3D scene: menus, HUD and text render, the world does not. The same game launched from Highball's library with d3dmetal works. The same black-3D symptom also showed up under DXVK (tried first, before switching). Performance needs DLSS to be usable: about 15 fps on the highest preset, 30 fps once DLSS Performance (MetalFX) is on.
